It serves enterprises across Communications, Manufacturing, BFSI, Technology/Media/Entertainment, Retail/Travel/Transportation & Logistics, and Healthcare & Life Sciences, and is part of the Mahindra Group, founded in 1945.

currentContext.strengths: Part of the Mahindra Group (founded 1945), one of the largest and most admired multinational federations of companies, providing brand lineage and ecosystem access.|Full-stack, integrated service portfolio spanning consulting, IT, business process services, engineering, network services, customer experience & design, AI & analytics and cloud & infrastructure — cited as a core SWOT strength ('Full-stack service offerings').|Long-standing relationships with leading telecom operators and ecosystem partners across geographies, with capabilities spanning design, deployment, transformation and managed services across the network lifecycle.|AI-led capabilities and scaled industry expertise (SWOT strength), reinforced by proprietary platforms such as the TechM Orion agentic AI platform and large-scale workforce upskilling — 80,000+ associates enabled with AI/GenAI skills.|First Indian company awarded the Sustainable Markets Initiative's Terra Carta Seal; recognised as a Global Sustainability Leader in the S&P Global DJSI and the only Indian IT company with an 'A' rating across all three CDP categories (Climate Change, Water Security, Supplier Engagement).|Industry-highest Net Promoter Score (NPS), cited by management as reflecting client trust.
currentContext.strategies: "AI Delivered Right" is TechM's core operating strategy — organising how delivery teams are structured and trained, how service lines invest, and how clients evaluate the company, built on four pillars: Transformation Delivered, Productivity Delivered, Innovation Delivered, and Assurance Delivered.|TechM Orion, the company's enterprise-grade agentic AI platform, is the execution vehicle for the AI Delivered Right strategy, unifying agent design, orchestration, governance and scaling across the enterprise stack.|Evolving commercial models for the AI era: 'Vector Squads' (composable delivery units of agents plus human experts priced by outcome, not headcount) and 'Service Tokens' (consumption-based commercial units for AI-led services) — a shift from billable hours to outcome/consumption pricing.|Project Fortius continues to drive operational rigor through disciplined cost management, improved utilisation, optimised delivery structures, and enhanced billing realisation.|Turbocharge program continues to drive disciplined account mining and execution across existing large accounts, with a differentiated operating approach focused on hygiene, performance, governance and reporting.|Customer-centricity strategy anchored on the Must Have Accounts (MHA) program, using focused account playbooks for deeper CXO engagement, stronger solution mapping and accelerated new-logo acquisition in priority markets.|Continued scale-up of investment in 'TechM Consulting' and Global Capability Centre (GCC)-related offerings, both cited as already delivering tangible business impact and strengthening strategic positioning.|Large-scale workforce upskilling in AI and Generative AI (80,000+ associates enabled) to align talent capability with evolving client demand and embed AI within large transformation programs.|Sustained focus on high-growth service lines, prioritised markets, disciplined capital allocation, and integration of acquired portfolio companies to advance toward FY27 profitability objectives under the FY27 roadmap.|Continued expansion of the ESG-led service portfolio — ESG advisory and consulting, resource and energy management, EHS risk management, regulatory compliance and incident tracking, and supply-chain/ESG reporting platforms.|Per its Dividend Distribution Policy (Regulation 43A, SEBI Listing Regulations), TechM commits to a minimum payout ratio of 85% or more of free cash flow generated over a five-year period, distributed as dividends and/or buybacks; the payout is determined based on available financial resources and investment requirements, reflecting a stated commitment to delivering shareholder value and optimal returns. For FY26 the Board confirmed an Interim Dividend of ₹15 per equity share (300% of face value, paid November 2025) and recommended a Final Dividend of ₹36 per equity share (720% of face value).
currentContext.expansion: As an asset-light global IT services and consulting business, TechM's 'expansion' in FY26 was expressed through capability and footprint build-out rather than physical plant capacity: deepening aerospace & defence capabilities within Manufacturing to offset automotive softness; scaling the BFSI portfolio-company offerings (payments, asset & wealth management, core banking, insurance platforms) and launching i.GreenFinance; continued investment scale-up in 'TechM Consulting' and Global Capability Centre (GCC)-related offerings; and integration of acquired portfolio companies across front-, middle- and back-office functions. On the sustainable-procurement side, TechM has set a goal to evaluate the top 250 of its high-spend key suppliers by 2030 for regulatory, ethical and sustainability compliance. Under BRSR Principle 2, the company disclosed that capital expenditure directed toward environmentally/socially beneficial technologies (infrastructure, energy and water efficiency initiatives) was 2.12% of total capex in FY26, down from 2.55% in FY25, while comparable R&D spend (AI, Cloud, Innovation and core R&D) rose to 33.2% of total R&D from 30% in FY25.
currentContext.mdna: Structural demand drivers — digital modernisation, cloud adoption, and AI-enabled transformation — continue to underpin medium-to-long-term IT services industry fundamentals even as near-term spending is more phased and prioritised.|Enterprise GenAI adoption is maturing: interest remains strong but enterprises are more selective, prioritising use cases with clearer links to operational efficiency, cost optimisation and scalability; legacy-system modernisation for AI readiness is expected to expand the addressable market over time.|Agentic AI is gaining momentum, with enterprises beginning to explore agent-based workflows for targeted efficiency improvements.|Global Capability Centres (GCCs) are maturing beyond scale expansion toward higher-value, more integrated mandates, creating a continued partner role for IT services companies in governance frameworks, digital platforms and operating models.|FY26 consolidated revenue growth was primarily driven by strong performance in the Manufacturing and BFSI verticals, with additional momentum from Retail, Travel and Logistics, supported by deeper engagement in existing accounts and ramp-up/scaling of new client wins.|Communications vertical: multi-year strategic engagements entered with leading European telecommunications service providers focused on innovation, digital resilience and AI-led operational efficiencies; AI-led offerings are enhancing the company's 'right to win' with telecom clients.|Manufacturing vertical: global automotive sector remains challenged, prompting a proactive shift toward aerospace and defence, construction, energy & utilities and mining, with focus on Industry 4.0, smart factory and IoT-enabled solutions.|BFSI vertical: financial institutions remain focused on operational resilience while selectively advancing transformation programs tied to efficiency and risk management; niche strength in payments, asset & wealth management, core banking and insurance platforms.|Industry outlook for FY26/FY27 reflects cautious optimism and a measured growth trajectory amid macroeconomic uncertainty and elevated tariffs; external industry advisors place FY27 IT-services growth expectations broadly in the 2-5% range.|Direct revenue exposure to geopolitically affected regions (e.g. Middle East conflict zones) is a low single-digit percentage of overall revenue and is not expected to be material.|Large deal bookings heading into FY27 are at their highest level in over a decade for TechM, reflecting a well-balanced mix across verticals and geographies.|Total deal wins of USD 3.79 billion in FY26, a 42% year-on-year increase, including closure of large and strategic deals and continued diversification of revenue mix across markets, industries and service lines.|Highest LTM (last-twelve-month) deal wins in a decade, even amid continued macroeconomic uncertainty.|Top accounts continue to outpace overall organisational growth, supported by a robust pipeline driven through structured account planning, focused leadership interventions, and deep account-mining initiatives.|$20 million+ accounts under the Turbocharge program are achieving quarterly run rates exceeding $1 billion and growing faster than the company average.

risks.note: Reduced client spend from adverse business conditions, competitive loss, or global economic slowdown/recession — including geopolitical conflicts such as the Middle East wars, GDP/inflation/interest-rate headwinds and trade wars — could adversely impact revenue growth; management notes direct revenue exposure to affected regions is only a low single-digit percentage of overall revenue.

risks.risk: Cyber security and data privacy risk
risks.note: Risk of data theft, information-security deviations and cyber attacks; unauthorized use or disclosure of employee, company or customer data could breach customer contracts, trigger regulatory fines/penalties, or damage reputation.

Possibility of declining business performance at acquired portfolio companies, due to a weak economic environment or strategic/operational factors, leading to impairment; inability or delay in integrating acquisitions to achieve synergies could cause financial losses, reputational damage, reduced productivity or legal matters.

High attrition levels, involuntary churn, leadership/organisational change, and work-from-home productivity and data-security risks could adversely impact resource deployment on new and existing projects.
Tracking constantly changing compliance requirements across multiple geographies and legal entities is a challenge; non-compliance could damage reputation or result in penal action by regulators.

Inability to timely adopt or invest in emerging technological competencies could create a competitive disadvantage; developing or acquiring new technologies and organisation-wide adoption carries significant cost implications.
Inherent project-level risk of not delivering on time, within budget, or to customer specifications, which could lead to penalties, loss of business, or reputational damage.
Legal, litigation and contractual risk arising from contract execution and matters relating to IPR, tax, regulations, employment contracts, adverse rulings, and mergers.

one-line thesis: The turnaround is delivering on schedule in its "final year": revenue US$1.66bn (+6.6% YoY CC), the strongest growth since the transformation began, with EVERY vertical growing YoY and manufacturing +17.2% YoY (aerospace + an accelerated European-auto program). Operating margin 14.4% (+330bps YoY, 11th consecutive quarter of expansion), TCV US$1.078bn (+33% YoY, third straight >$1bn), FCF +94% YoY, ROCE 28.3% (+450bps YoY). Management reaffirms the FY27 goalposts: growth above peer average (already achieved in Q1) and a 15% operating margin (exit Q4 >15%). Project Helix (agentic-AI, 350+ agents, Orion platform) is the growth engine; Project Fortius the margin engine. Near-term watch: a ~1–1.3% European-auto revenue pull-forward reverses in Q2, wage hikes land Q2, and AI productivity pressures pricing — but large-deal ramps are guided to offset.

> **Distortions:** (1) Manufacturing's QoQ +9% flattered by EARLY execution of a large European-auto program — a ~1–1.3% revenue benefit that will NOT repeat and pressures Q2. (2) Q1 seasonally weak on Comviva → reported growth muted by Comviva seasonality + a one-time client cloud-consumption insourcing (pass-through going direct post-acquisition). (3) TME declined -1.7% QoQ on client-spend volatility. (4) Effective tax 27.2%; hedge-book MTM -US$24.85mn (US$14.55mn P&L / US$10.3mn reserves). (5) Margin expansion this quarter led by SG&A (portfolio-company consolidation); gross-margin levers (Fortius, FP productivity, T&M utilisation) still ahead.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **FY27 growth:** above peer-average (already ahead in Q1; "meet or exceed"); Rohit framed it as delivering high-single-digit YoY growth. No specific number given ("foolhardy" amid volatility).
- **FY27 operating margin:** 15% target; exit Q4FY27 "upwards of 15%." Beyond FY27 margin path to be spelled out later.
- **European-auto pull-forward:** ~1–1.3% negative revenue impact in Q2 (won't repeat); offset by large-deal ramp-ups + base business.
- **Comms & Manufacturing:** both to GROW YoY through the remainder of the year (Comviva seasonality + cloud pass-through headwinds reverse in Q2).
- **Wage hikes:** effective Q2FY27, phased.
- **IT-services headcount:** down 7% YoY (AI-driven FP productivity, not revenue decline); expects to HIRE in the remainder of FY27 (fresh + experienced).
- **Onsite-offshore pyramid:** offshore-shift margin lever LIMITED this year (large-deal rebadge + onsite-heavy SAP/ServiceNow/Salesforce work); reduction expected in later years, "not in this year."
order book & pipeline:
- TCV US$1.078bn (+33% YoY), broad-based; largest wins Manufacturing + HLS. Third consecutive $1bn+ quarter. ISG named TechM among top-15 sourcing standouts (all regions).
- Notable wins: US regional healthcare system (integrated apps + infra managed services); American autonomous-driving co (HD map dev/maintenance via GIS); global aerospace & defense (database admin + AI ops); global payments-technology co (product engineering); marquee AI-led BPS deal with a large high-tech player (one of the largest AI-led BPS deals).
- Large-deal forecast visibility limited to ~1–2 quarters (binary win/loss); pipeline "quite strong."
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Vertical YoY growth:** Manufacturing +17.2% (leader; +9% QoQ), BFSI +8.1%, Retail-Travel-Logistics +8.6%, Healthcare +7.2%, Communications +1.3%; TME -1.7% QoQ. Every vertical grew YoY.
- **Portfolio cos:** Comviva — revenue growth, improved margins, healthy order book (but Q1 seasonal negative); Pininfarina — preparing AI-led transformation of mobility/architecture businesses.
- **Acquisition:** Avant Techno Solutions (Canada) — payments modernization + wealth platforms; deepens BFSI payments/wealth (structurally high-growth, faster than traditional IT).
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Project Helix (AI-led transformation):** platforms + talent + partnerships in one operating model; agentic development & modernization services portfolio launched; TechM Orion (multi-agent orchestration) — 20+ agents on Google Gemini marketplace, 100+ active users; 350+ deployable AI agents; TechM Scale for vendor-consolidation.
- **AI-first across IT + BPS:** outcome-linked deals (healthcare: ~40% fewer tickets, 20% lower MTTR, 30–35% tech-debt cut; telecom: ~2x release velocity, ~40% incident-effort cut). AI ops = "overwhelming majority" of BPS deal TCV this quarter.
- **Partnerships:** Microsoft (5G network digital-twin), Kitsa (agentic medical writing), Telefonica Germany (multi-year AI-first private cloud), Perplexity Enterprise Pro (internal deployment).
- **Domain + sovereign AI:** purpose-built industry models (telecom SLMs w/ agentic harness) — mgmt's stated future differentiator (marry AI onto deep vertical/process knowledge).
- **Demand strengthening:** ServiceNow, SAP, Salesforce; data & AI (Databricks, Snowflake, GenAI); vertical packages (Guidewire, Temenos, LabWare LIMS). "SaaS eclipse" fear NOT materialising — enterprise-app demand strengthening.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Comms/telecom depth:** full-stack across OSS/BSS + networks + own software packages; ability to build a telecom SLM from scratch AND fit an agentic action-harness onto it — cited as a genuine, hard-to-replicate differentiator.
- **Vertical "special sauce":** deep domain expertise (payments/wealth/insurance in BFSI; life-sciences/provider in healthcare; aerospace in manufacturing) layered with agentic-AI frameworks — mgmt attributes the differentiated growth to vertical depth, not horizontal tooling alone.
- **Pricing discipline as a moat:** deliberately walks away from "irrational" competitor terms (70–80% productivity over 5-yr deals; guaranteeing memory/chip prices amid 20% YoY inflation) — protects long-term margin accretion.
- **Recognitions:** 2026 Google Cloud Partner of the Year (manufacturing); Time's most sustainable (No.1 Indian corporate); Frost & Sullivan (Orion Marketplace).
margins & cost dynamics:
- 14.4% EBIT (+330bps YoY): driven by volume growth + Project Fortius savings; partially offset by Comviva seasonality + business mix. This quarter's expansion was SG&A-led (portfolio-company consolidation).
- Gross-margin levers still in hand: FP productivity, higher T&M utilisation, continued Fortius actions — "mix of both" (GM + SG&A) into coming quarters, all pointed at the 15% target.
- Q1 gross margin carried seasonal negatives: visa/travel costs (Q4→Q1), Comviva seasonality, dilutive European-auto accelerated deliveries.
- Headwinds ahead: Q2 wage bill + AI-driven productivity pass-through pressure on pricing.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): - Not a physical-capex story. Investment in AI capabilities, IP, software licenses, talent, and centres-of-excellence (Comms CoE Pune; Hyderabad learning/engineering/retail-CPG CoEs) — calibrated to where growth opportunities are. No commissioning dates to track.
capital allocation: - Disciplined deal selection (all deals long-term margin-accretive); continued investment in talent/IP/software licenses, calibrated to growth. FCF +94% YoY (US$167mn), ROCE 28.3% — strong capital efficiency. Portfolio-company consolidation/liquidation of underperformers continues (SG&A benefit). No specific dividend/buyback commentary this call.
risks & watch-items:
- **European-auto pull-forward reversal** (~1–1.3% Q2 revenue drag) — must be offset by large-deal ramps + base performance.
- **Wage bill (Q2)** + **AI productivity pressure** on pricing — margin discipline "not taken for granted."
- **Comms volatility** — a large US telecom client volatile; cloud pass-through pullback (reverses Q2).
- **Competition "irrational"** on productivity/price guarantees — a demand-quality risk if TechM must match to win.
- **Memory/chip inflation ~20% YoY** — refuses to guarantee for 3–5-yr deals.
- **Client contract-signing delays** — one or two multi-year examples (in-house vs outsource, AI-benefit questions); mgmt says "not different from 25+ years" and no outsized cancellations. No ramp-up delays worth worrying about.
- **Demand-challenged areas:** manual testing, traditional big data, standalone e-commerce, legacy CRM, legacy infra admin.
management quality / tone: Confident but disciplined — "final year of transformation," proud of the journey, yet repeatedly refuses to give specific growth numbers ("foolhardy" / "hard to forecast beyond a quarter or two"), which reads as credible given large-deal binary-outcome candor. Mohit Joshi (25+ yrs industry) is precise on demand nuances (winners vs challenged areas) and openly names competitor "irrationality" with concrete examples. CFO Rohit Anand quantifies headwinds cleanly (European-auto 1–1.3% Q2). Overall: high-quality, numbers-grounded, low-hype.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **Growth quality > the print:** the strong quarter was partly an auto pull-forward (~1–1.3%), so the "clean" run-rate is a touch lower — but every vertical grew YoY and the large-deal ramp (not yet started) is the real Q2+ driver.
- **The margin story is shifting composition:** Q1 expansion was SG&A-led (portfolio consolidation); gross-margin levers (Fortius/FP-productivity/T&M-utilisation) are still largely UNSPENT — supportive of the 15% exit even against wage + AI-pricing headwinds.
- **Headcount down 7% YoY is NOT a demand signal** — it's AI-driven FP productivity + repurposing; hiring resumes in H2. Onsite-offshore pyramid lever is deferred (rebadge + onsite-heavy SAP/ServiceNow) — a margin lever for LATER years, not FY27.
- **"SaaS eclipse" explicitly rejected** — enterprise-app (SAP/ServiceNow/Salesforce) demand strengthening; a useful counter-read to bearish IT-services SaaS-disruption narratives.
- **AI is both opportunity and operating-model risk** — some traditional work compresses/needs new commercial constructs (token economics, AI FinOps, outcome-linked delivery) even as new demand expands.

one-line thesis: The turnaround is delivering on schedule in its "final year": revenue US$1.66bn (+6.6% YoY CC), the strongest growth since the transformation began, with EVERY vertical growing YoY and manufacturing +17.2% YoY (aerospace + an accelerated European-auto program). Operating margin 14.4% (+330bps YoY, 11th consecutive quarter of expansion), TCV US$1.078bn (+33% YoY, third straight >$1bn), FCF +94% YoY, ROCE 28.3% (+450bps YoY). Management reaffirms the FY27 goalposts: growth above peer average (already achieved in Q1) and a 15% operating margin (exit Q4 >15%). Project Helix (agentic-AI, 350+ agents, Orion platform) is the growth engine; Project Fortius the margin engine. Near-term watch: a ~1–1.3% European-auto revenue pull-forward reverses in Q2, wage hikes land Q2, and AI productivity pressures pricing — but large-deal ramps are guided to offset.

> **Distortions:** (1) Manufacturing's QoQ +9% flattered by EARLY execution of a large European-auto program — a ~1–1.3% revenue benefit that will NOT repeat and pressures Q2. (2) Q1 seasonally weak on Comviva → reported growth muted by Comviva seasonality + a one-time client cloud-consumption insourcing (pass-through going direct post-acquisition). (3) TME declined -1.7% QoQ on client-spend volatility. (4) Effective tax 27.2%; hedge-book MTM -US$24.85mn (US$14.55mn P&L / US$10.3mn reserves). (5) Margin expansion this quarter led by SG&A (portfolio-company consolidation); gross-margin levers (Fortius, FP productivity, T&M utilisation) still ahead.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **FY27 growth:** above peer-average (already ahead in Q1; "meet or exceed"); Rohit framed it as delivering high-single-digit YoY growth. No specific number given ("foolhardy" amid volatility).
- **FY27 operating margin:** 15% target; exit Q4FY27 "upwards of 15%." Beyond FY27 margin path to be spelled out later.
- **European-auto pull-forward:** ~1–1.3% negative revenue impact in Q2 (won't repeat); offset by large-deal ramp-ups + base business.
- **Comms & Manufacturing:** both to GROW YoY through the remainder of the year (Comviva seasonality + cloud pass-through headwinds reverse in Q2).
- **Wage hikes:** effective Q2FY27, phased.
- **IT-services headcount:** down 7% YoY (AI-driven FP productivity, not revenue decline); expects to HIRE in the remainder of FY27 (fresh + experienced).
- **Onsite-offshore pyramid:** offshore-shift margin lever LIMITED this year (large-deal rebadge + onsite-heavy SAP/ServiceNow/Salesforce work); reduction expected in later years, "not in this year."
order book & pipeline:
- TCV US$1.078bn (+33% YoY), broad-based; largest wins Manufacturing + HLS. Third consecutive $1bn+ quarter. ISG named TechM among top-15 sourcing standouts (all regions).
- Notable wins: US regional healthcare system (integrated apps + infra managed services); American autonomous-driving co (HD map dev/maintenance via GIS); global aerospace & defense (database admin + AI ops); global payments-technology co (product engineering); marquee AI-led BPS deal with a large high-tech player (one of the largest AI-led BPS deals).
- Large-deal forecast visibility limited to ~1–2 quarters (binary win/loss); pipeline "quite strong."
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Vertical YoY growth:** Manufacturing +17.2% (leader; +9% QoQ), BFSI +8.1%, Retail-Travel-Logistics +8.6%, Healthcare +7.2%, Communications +1.3%; TME -1.7% QoQ. Every vertical grew YoY.
- **Portfolio cos:** Comviva — revenue growth, improved margins, healthy order book (but Q1 seasonal negative); Pininfarina — preparing AI-led transformation of mobility/architecture businesses.
- **Acquisition:** Avant Techno Solutions (Canada) — payments modernization + wealth platforms; deepens BFSI payments/wealth (structurally high-growth, faster than traditional IT).
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Project Helix (AI-led transformation):** platforms + talent + partnerships in one operating model; agentic development & modernization services portfolio launched; TechM Orion (multi-agent orchestration) — 20+ agents on Google Gemini marketplace, 100+ active users; 350+ deployable AI agents; TechM Scale for vendor-consolidation.
- **AI-first across IT + BPS:** outcome-linked deals (healthcare: ~40% fewer tickets, 20% lower MTTR, 30–35% tech-debt cut; telecom: ~2x release velocity, ~40% incident-effort cut). AI ops = "overwhelming majority" of BPS deal TCV this quarter.
- **Partnerships:** Microsoft (5G network digital-twin), Kitsa (agentic medical writing), Telefonica Germany (multi-year AI-first private cloud), Perplexity Enterprise Pro (internal deployment).
- **Domain + sovereign AI:** purpose-built industry models (telecom SLMs w/ agentic harness) — mgmt's stated future differentiator (marry AI onto deep vertical/process knowledge).
- **Demand strengthening:** ServiceNow, SAP, Salesforce; data & AI (Databricks, Snowflake, GenAI); vertical packages (Guidewire, Temenos, LabWare LIMS). "SaaS eclipse" fear NOT materialising — enterprise-app demand strengthening.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Comms/telecom depth:** full-stack across OSS/BSS + networks + own software packages; ability to build a telecom SLM from scratch AND fit an agentic action-harness onto it — cited as a genuine, hard-to-replicate differentiator.
- **Vertical "special sauce":** deep domain expertise (payments/wealth/insurance in BFSI; life-sciences/provider in healthcare; aerospace in manufacturing) layered with agentic-AI frameworks — mgmt attributes the differentiated growth to vertical depth, not horizontal tooling alone.
- **Pricing discipline as a moat:** deliberately walks away from "irrational" competitor terms (70–80% productivity over 5-yr deals; guaranteeing memory/chip prices amid 20% YoY inflation) — protects long-term margin accretion.
- **Recognitions:** 2026 Google Cloud Partner of the Year (manufacturing); Time's most sustainable (No.1 Indian corporate); Frost & Sullivan (Orion Marketplace).
margins & cost dynamics:
- 14.4% EBIT (+330bps YoY): driven by volume growth + Project Fortius savings; partially offset by Comviva seasonality + business mix. This quarter's expansion was SG&A-led (portfolio-company consolidation).
- Gross-margin levers still in hand: FP productivity, higher T&M utilisation, continued Fortius actions — "mix of both" (GM + SG&A) into coming quarters, all pointed at the 15% target.
- Q1 gross margin carried seasonal negatives: visa/travel costs (Q4→Q1), Comviva seasonality, dilutive European-auto accelerated deliveries.
- Headwinds ahead: Q2 wage bill + AI-driven productivity pass-through pressure on pricing.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): - Not a physical-capex story. Investment in AI capabilities, IP, software licenses, talent, and centres-of-excellence (Comms CoE Pune; Hyderabad learning/engineering/retail-CPG CoEs) — calibrated to where growth opportunities are. No commissioning dates to track.
capital allocation: - Disciplined deal selection (all deals long-term margin-accretive); continued investment in talent/IP/software licenses, calibrated to growth. FCF +94% YoY (US$167mn), ROCE 28.3% — strong capital efficiency. Portfolio-company consolidation/liquidation of underperformers continues (SG&A benefit). No specific dividend/buyback commentary this call.
risks & watch-items:
- **European-auto pull-forward reversal** (~1–1.3% Q2 revenue drag) — must be offset by large-deal ramps + base performance.
- **Wage bill (Q2)** + **AI productivity pressure** on pricing — margin discipline "not taken for granted."
- **Comms volatility** — a large US telecom client volatile; cloud pass-through pullback (reverses Q2).
- **Competition "irrational"** on productivity/price guarantees — a demand-quality risk if TechM must match to win.
- **Memory/chip inflation ~20% YoY** — refuses to guarantee for 3–5-yr deals.
- **Client contract-signing delays** — one or two multi-year examples (in-house vs outsource, AI-benefit questions); mgmt says "not different from 25+ years" and no outsized cancellations. No ramp-up delays worth worrying about.
- **Demand-challenged areas:** manual testing, traditional big data, standalone e-commerce, legacy CRM, legacy infra admin.
management quality / tone: Confident but disciplined — "final year of transformation," proud of the journey, yet repeatedly refuses to give specific growth numbers ("foolhardy" / "hard to forecast beyond a quarter or two"), which reads as credible given large-deal binary-outcome candor. Mohit Joshi (25+ yrs industry) is precise on demand nuances (winners vs challenged areas) and openly names competitor "irrationality" with concrete examples. CFO Rohit Anand quantifies headwinds cleanly (European-auto 1–1.3% Q2). Overall: high-quality, numbers-grounded, low-hype.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **Growth quality > the print:** the strong quarter was partly an auto pull-forward (~1–1.3%), so the "clean" run-rate is a touch lower — but every vertical grew YoY and the large-deal ramp (not yet started) is the real Q2+ driver.
- **The margin story is shifting composition:** Q1 expansion was SG&A-led (portfolio consolidation); gross-margin levers (Fortius/FP-productivity/T&M-utilisation) are still largely UNSPENT — supportive of the 15% exit even against wage + AI-pricing headwinds.
- **Headcount down 7% YoY is NOT a demand signal** — it's AI-driven FP productivity + repurposing; hiring resumes in H2. Onsite-offshore pyramid lever is deferred (rebadge + onsite-heavy SAP/ServiceNow) — a margin lever for LATER years, not FY27.
- **"SaaS eclipse" explicitly rejected** — enterprise-app (SAP/ServiceNow/Salesforce) demand strengthening; a useful counter-read to bearish IT-services SaaS-disruption narratives.
- **AI is both opportunity and operating-model risk** — some traditional work compresses/needs new commercial constructs (token economics, AI FinOps, outcome-linked delivery) even as new demand expands.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural demand drivers — digital modernisation, cloud adoption, and AI-enabled transformation — continue to underpin medium-to-long-term IT services industry fundamentals even as near-term spending is more phased and prioritised.
- Enterprise GenAI adoption is maturing: interest remains strong but enterprises are more selective, prioritising use cases with clearer links to operational efficiency, cost optimisation and scalability; legacy-system modernisation for AI readiness is expected to expand the addressable market over time.
- Agentic AI is gaining momentum, with enterprises beginning to explore agent-based workflows for targeted efficiency improvements.
- Global Capability Centres (GCCs) are maturing beyond scale expansion toward higher-value, more integrated mandates, creating a continued partner role for IT services companies in governance frameworks, digital platforms and operating models.
- FY26 consolidated revenue growth was primarily driven by strong performance in the Manufacturing and BFSI verticals, with additional momentum from Retail, Travel and Logistics, supported by deeper engagement in existing accounts and ramp-up/scaling of new client wins.
- Communications vertical: multi-year strategic engagements entered with leading European telecommunications service providers focused on innovation, digital resilience and AI-led operational efficiencies; AI-led offerings are enhancing the company's 'right to win' with telecom clients.
- Manufacturing vertical: global automotive sector remains challenged, prompting a proactive shift toward aerospace and defence, construction, energy & utilities and mining, with focus on Industry 4.0, smart factory and IoT-enabled solutions.
- BFSI vertical: financial institutions remain focused on operational resilience while selectively advancing transformation programs tied to efficiency and risk management; niche strength in payments, asset & wealth management, core banking and insurance platforms.
- Industry outlook for FY26/FY27 reflects cautious optimism and a measured growth trajectory amid macroeconomic uncertainty and elevated tariffs; external industry advisors place FY27 IT-services growth expectations broadly in the 2-5% range.
- Direct revenue exposure to geopolitically affected regions (e.g. Middle East conflict zones) is a low single-digit percentage of overall revenue and is not expected to be material.
- Large deal bookings heading into FY27 are at their highest level in over a decade for TechM, reflecting a well-balanced mix across verticals and geographies.
- Total deal wins of USD 3.79 billion in FY26, a 42% year-on-year increase, including closure of large and strategic deals and continued diversification of revenue mix across markets, industries and service lines.
- Highest LTM (last-twelve-month) deal wins in a decade, even amid continued macroeconomic uncertainty.
- Top accounts continue to outpace overall organisational growth, supported by a robust pipeline driven through structured account planning, focused leadership interventions, and deep account-mining initiatives.
- $20 million+ accounts under the Turbocharge program are achieving quarterly run rates exceeding $1 billion and growing faster than the company average.

- Gross-margin levers still in hand: FP productivity, higher T&M utilisation, continued Fortius actions — "mix of both" (GM + SG&A) into coming quarters, all pointed at the 15% target.
- Q1 gross margin carried seasonal negatives: visa/travel costs (Q4→Q1), Comviva seasonality, dilutive European-auto accelerated deliveries.
- Headwinds ahead: Q2 wage bill + AI-driven productivity pass-through pressure on pricing.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: - Disciplined deal selection (all deals long-term margin-accretive); continued investment in talent/IP/software licenses, calibrated to growth. FCF +94% YoY (US$167mn), ROCE 28.3% — strong capital efficiency. Portfolio-company consolidation/liquidation of underperformers continues (SG&A benefit). No specific dividend/buyback commentary this call.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: As an asset-light global IT services and consulting business, TechM's 'expansion' in FY26 was expressed through capability and footprint build-out rather than physical plant capacity: deepening aerospace & defence capabilities within Manufacturing to offset automotive softness; scaling the BFSI portfolio-company offerings (payments, asset & wealth management, core banking, insurance platforms) and launching i.GreenFinance; continued investment scale-up in 'TechM Consulting' and Global Capability Centre (GCC)-related offerings; and integration of acquired portfolio companies across front-, middle- and back-office functions. On the sustainable-procurement side, TechM has set a goal to evaluate the top 250 of its high-spend key suppliers by 2030 for regulatory, ethical and sustainability compliance. Under BRSR Principle 2, the company disclosed that capital expenditure directed toward environmentally/socially beneficial technologies (infrastructure, energy and water efficiency initiatives) was 2.12% of total capex in FY26, down from 2.55% in FY25, while comparable R&D spend (AI, Cloud, Innovation and core R&D) rose to 33.2% of total R&D from 30% in FY25.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident but disciplined — "final year of transformation," proud of the journey, yet repeatedly refuses to give specific growth numbers ("foolhardy" / "hard to forecast beyond a quarter or two"), which reads as credible given large-deal binary-outcome candor. Mohit Joshi (25+ yrs industry) is precise on demand nuances (winners vs challenged areas) and openly names competitor "irrationality" with concrete examples. CFO Rohit Anand quantifies headwinds cleanly (European-auto 1–1.3% Q2). Overall: high-quality, numbers-grounded, low-hype.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Part of the Mahindra Group (founded 1945), one of the largest and most admired multinational federations of companies, providing brand lineage and ecosystem access.
- Full-stack, integrated service portfolio spanning consulting, IT, business process services, engineering, network services, customer experience & design, AI & analytics and cloud & infrastructure — cited as a core SWOT strength ('Full-stack service offerings').
- Long-standing relationships with leading telecom operators and ecosystem partners across geographies, with capabilities spanning design, deployment, transformation and managed services across the network lifecycle.
- AI-led capabilities and scaled industry expertise (SWOT strength), reinforced by proprietary platforms such as the TechM Orion agentic AI platform and large-scale workforce upskilling — 80,000+ associates enabled with AI/GenAI skills.
- First Indian company awarded the Sustainable Markets Initiative's Terra Carta Seal; recognised as a Global Sustainability Leader in the S&P Global DJSI and the only Indian IT company with an 'A' rating across all three CDP categories (Climate Change, Water Security, Supplier Engagement).
- Industry-highest Net Promoter Score (NPS), cited by management as reflecting client trust.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **European-auto pull-forward reversal** (~1–1.3% Q2 revenue drag) — must be offset by large-deal ramps + base performance.
- **Wage bill (Q2)** + **AI productivity pressure** on pricing — margin discipline "not taken for granted."
- **Comms volatility** — a large US telecom client volatile; cloud pass-through pullback (reverses Q2).
- **Competition "irrational"** on productivity/price guarantees — a demand-quality risk if TechM must match to win.
- **Memory/chip inflation ~20% YoY** — refuses to guarantee for 3–5-yr deals.
- **Client contract-signing delays** — one or two multi-year examples (in-house vs outsource, AI-benefit questions); mgmt says "not different from 25+ years" and no outsized cancellations. No ramp-up delays worth worrying about.
- **Demand-challenged areas:** manual testing, traditional big data, standalone e-commerce, legacy CRM, legacy infra admin.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **Growth quality > the print:** the strong quarter was partly an auto pull-forward (~1–1.3%), so the "clean" run-rate is a touch lower — but every vertical grew YoY and the large-deal ramp (not yet started) is the real Q2+ driver.
- **The margin story is shifting composition:** Q1 expansion was SG&A-led (portfolio consolidation); gross-margin levers (Fortius/FP-productivity/T&M-utilisation) are still largely UNSPENT — supportive of the 15% exit even against wage + AI-pricing headwinds.
- **Headcount down 7% YoY is NOT a demand signal** — it's AI-driven FP productivity + repurposing; hiring resumes in H2. Onsite-offshore pyramid lever is deferred (rebadge + onsite-heavy SAP/ServiceNow) — a margin lever for LATER years, not FY27.
- **"SaaS eclipse" explicitly rejected** — enterprise-app (SAP/ServiceNow/Salesforce) demand strengthening; a useful counter-read to bearish IT-services SaaS-disruption narratives.
- **AI is both opportunity and operating-model risk** — some traditional work compresses/needs new commercial constructs (token economics, AI FinOps, outcome-linked delivery) even as new demand expands.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Litigation - erstwhile Satyam] Claims made by 37 companies in the City Civil Court for alleged advances amounting to Rs. 12,304 Million are presented separately under "Suspense Account (net)"; management, on the basis of current legal status, lack of documentation and external legal opinion, believes these claims will not be payable on final adjudication, and the auditor's opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.
- [Litigation - status] Of the 37 petitions before the City Civil Court, Secunderabad, "one petition has been converted into suit and balance 36 petitions are at various stages of pauperism/suit admission"; legal notices claimed the advances "together with damages/compensation @ 18% per annum till the date of repayment", and the Directorate of Enforcement under PMLA "had directed the erstwhile Satyam not to return the alleged advances until further instructions."
- [Regulation - New Labour Codes] "Effective November 21, 2025, the Government of India notified the four Labour Codes... consolidating 29 existing labour laws"; the Group, "considering the materiality and regulatory driven, non-recurring nature, presented the incremental impact of Rs. 2,724 Million related to Employee Benefit Obligations under 'Exceptional item'."
- [Audit opinion] B S R & Co. LLP issued Unmodified Audit Reports on both the Audited Consolidated and Standalone Financial Results for the quarter ended 30 June 2026, with an Emphasis of Matter on the erstwhile Satyam matters.
- [Governance] Board meeting held Thursday, 16th July 2026 commenced at 2.15 p.m. (IST) and concluded at 3.55 p.m. (IST), and was thereafter adjourned to be convened on Friday, 17th July 2026; results signed by Mohit Joshi, Managing Director & CEO.
